2. PROTOTYPE SITES
A. Indianapolis, Indiana
Site Developer: Urban Systems Development Corporation
Site Planner: Skidmore, Owings & Merrill
Housing Mix: 52 Multi-family low rise (MFLR)
140 Single-family attached (SFA) 103 Single-family detached (SFD)
Ownership Pattern: Private owners, rental units, some subsidy.
This site is located on the periphery of the city near the Indianpolis Speedway. The site area is 42.9 acres; an additional 10 acres of the original site proposal is being developed by the city for a public park. The site is part of a 120 acre farm originally operated by the Indiana Mental Health Department, until it was closed approximately two years ago.
Prior to Operation BREAKTHROUGH, the site was owned by the county, and used for the cultivation of crops. It was zoned for agricultural use. It is surrounded by a neighborhood of single family detached homes on a typical rectangular grid pattern. The topography is flat.
The site design provides cluster planning of the various housing elements, with extensive site grading to develop visual interest and to provide storm water catchment basins. The site plan includes a conceptual plan for development of the rest of the 120 acre property.
B. Jersey City, New Jersey
Site Develope: Volt Information Sciences, Inc.
Site Planner: David A. Crane, Architect
Housing Mix: 434 Multi-family high rise
52 Multi-family low rise
Ownership Pattern: Non-profit rental, some subsidized.
This 6.35 acre inner-city site is located at the intersection of Newark Avenue and John F. Kennedy Boulevard, one block from the heart of the downtown area. The site has been vacant for several years, having been cleared as part of St. John's Urban Renewal Project Area.
The most outstanding characteristic of this site is the view of the panorama of the Manhattan skyline and the new York and Newark harbors. Downtown Manhattan is about 20 minutes away via rapid transit and the Port Authority Hudson Tubes.
